assumptions: The initial offer avoids providing unqualified legal opinions and uses qualified manual testers.
Covered SMEs will pay materially more for verified remediation evidence than for automated scans alone.
A useful share of sprint customers can be converted to recurring monitoring.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots showing covered SMEs purchase 6,000-25,000 PLN sprints, verified delivery hours and contribution margin, complaint or procurement urgency, and quarterly monitoring conversion and retention.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A fixed-scope Polish evidence-and-remediation sprint usefully bridges cheap automated scans and broad consultancies, though the gap is readily recognized and copied.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Covered businesses face real remediation and evidence work after the law took effect, but enforcement urgency, covered-SME incidence, and Polish spending remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Upfront sprint payments and plausible 55-70% contribution margins support bootstrapping; delivery remains labor-heavy and monitoring conversion, CAC, retention, and owner earnings are assumptions.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish covered digital-service SMEs are identifiable, but exemptions and the unknown covered population make the economically meaningful beachhead uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local language and standardized proof packs provide focus, but agencies, consultancies, and testing vendors can serve the same segment and bundle remediation.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Monitoring, release regression testing, additional regulated journeys, and CEE localization offer logical adjacencies after winning initial accounts.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Templates, harnesses, and defect benchmarks may improve delivery, but standards and scanning tools are public and customer switching costs appear modest.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A bounded, verified remediation outcome is more useful than a scanner report, but no demonstrated step-change in cost, speed, or assurance is supplied.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The recently effective Polish accessibility regime creates a credible current trigger, although actual enforcement intensity is unknown.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Public-site screening enables targeted prospecting and agency referrals could scale, but no owned customer channel or conversion evidence exists.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder can build the harness part-time with limited capital, while specialist manual testing, legal scoping, liability, and authenticated access add manageable dependencies.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a repeatable agency or insurer referral channel paired with a standardized remediation guarantee and recurring release-monitoring contract.
main_structural_strength: An owned, low-capital testing workflow can turn a current regulatory requirement into an immediately sellable fixed-scope service.
primary_score_limiter: The service lacks a hard-to-copy advantage and has no evidence that enforcement urgency produces repeatable Polish SME demand at the assumed prices.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Inexpensive scanners and incumbent web agencies can bundle much of the workflow, while many SMEs may be exempt or outside scope.
